entries.title: Ezekiel 11:1
segments: Five and twenty men; these seem to represent the rulers of Judah.

entries.title: Ezekiel 11:2
segments:
vv 2-3. 
 
Carnal security and contempt of God's threatenings prepare the way for wicked counsels and mischievous devices.

entries.title: Ezekiel 11:3
segments: It is not near; the destruction of Jerusalem threatened by Jeremiah.  But we may better render the first clause by of the verse thus: "The time is not near to build houses," that is, in Babylon, according to the advice of Jeremiah.

They scornfully reject the idea of a long captivity in Babylon. 
 
  This city is the caldron, and we be the flesh; as the flesh remains in the caldron till cooked, so we shall remain till death in Jerusalem. We shall not be removed prematurely by captivity.  Compare
, where God threatens to bring them out of Jerusalem.

entries.title: Ezekiel 11:6
segments:
vv 6-12. 
 
God has appointed rulers for the defence of the innocent and the punishment of the guilty.  When they become the oppressors and destroyers of the people, he will take the cause of justice into his own hands, and destroy them and their possessions together.

entries.title: Ezekiel 11:7
segments:
Your slain--are the flesh; Jehovah gives a new turn to their figure.  The city boiling with violence and bloodshed is the caldron, and the murdered are the flesh in it. 
 
  Bring you forth; that is, violently and prematurely.

entries.title: Ezekiel 11:10
segments: In the border of Israel; the princes of Judah were slain at Riblah, on the borders of Palestine.

entries.title: Ezekiel 11:13
segments:
Died; the prophet sees in vision the death of Pelatiah, a leader among the Jewish princes--a sure token that they shall all be destroyed. 
 
We ought to be filled with fear and trembling in view of God's threatenings, knowing that he will execute them upon all who persevere in sin, without respect of persons.

entries.title: Ezekiel 11:15
segments:
Thy brethren--the men of they kindred; thy fellow-captives of the Jewish nation. 
 
  Get you far from the Lord; literslly, "Be far from the Lord." Those who remain in Jerusalem despise their countrymen who have gone into captivity, as far removed from God's presence, and no longer the objects of his care.  But God assures the prophet that he will bless the latter, while he destroys the former.  Compare

. 
 
vv 15-16. 
 
The Jews who remained at Jerusalem in Ezekiel's day, gloried in their outward privileges and relations to God, and despised their brethren who had gone into captivity; but God destroyed the former, while he blessed the latter, and restored them at the appointed time to their own home.  So he deals with man, abasing the proud and exalting the humble.

entries.title: Ezekiel 11:16
segments: A little sanctuary; little, answering to the fewness of their number.  Some render, "a sanctuary for a short time," that is, till their return from captivity.

entries.title: Ezekiel 11:17
segments:
vv 17-21. 
 
God's own glory is concerned in the perpetuation from age to age of his true worshippers.  The same judgments which destroy the wicked he will make efficacious for the purification of the "remnant according to the election of grace," and their increase in the fruits of righteousness.

entries.title: Ezekiel 11:20
segments: My people; the remnant, to whom the promises contained in

are made, represent "the Israel of God."  The fulfilment of these promises belongs not to any one period of time.  It began in the restoration under Ezra, Zerubbabel, and others, but its full accomplishment belongs to "the last days" of Zion's glory.

entries.title: Ezekiel 11:23
segments: The mountain--on the east side of the city; the mount of Olives.
